title: Overlord Movie 3: Sei Oukoku-hen
content:
Unless you are a casual watcher, this is a movie that will have you sit one out for sure. It has been said many times. Overlord is an antagonist story with so much violence, ruthlessness and troublesome gray-moral delima. But there is the main series, and then there is the Sacred Kingdom movie. This was dark man.

This movie covers canon material by the way. The fourth season skipped a couple of volumes from the light novel, so this movie slots nicely between episode 7 and 8. It’s such a shame it was not included in the season, but alas.

If you haven’t gotten the memo yet,Ainz is the lead of a regime that will stop at nothing to further its interests and agendas. For the sake of a good conversation regarding this movie, this review will not be holding on spoilers, so proceed at your own risk.

What might appear on the surface as the benevolent king, Ainz, offers his help to defeat the demon who threatens to wipe a kingdom off the face of the earth was actually a twisted Nazarick-run operation that revolved around destabilizing a peaceful kingdom’s politics, nuking civilians, using children as war shields, mass starvation and enslavement and rebranding the villain as the savior on top of it. Ainz was cooperating with the whole master plan that played both sides, and to what end? Trying to throw a sales pitch for rune technology. A reoccurring joke throughout the entire run of the movie, with awkward reactions whenever it’s brought up.

We could stop there or we could make a link with how real world mega corporation influence politics that can lead to mass human tragedies for more profit. A very sad and very real modern delima.

A round of applause for MadHouse on the consistent visual quality they had throughout this entire run. The fights, the panoramic shots, even the small talk moments, they all got the care they deserved. Topple it with matching voice acting and crisp SFX, and you have a visual-audible feast that does not let you down.

This was a surprising feast, deeper than I originally gave credits to. Some of the best Overlord content in my opinion. It carries a lot of weight and strikes a perfect metaphor to very humane issues.

Overall: 7.94/10.
